requirement.summary: Provider callback identity and UNKNOWN reconciliation create at most one terminal login result and session family.
Refresh is single-use and reuse atomically revokes the complete token family.
Device trust binds fingerprint user nonce and expiry and revocation invalidates derived identity.
Key rotation has one ACTIVE issuer, a bounded RETIRING verifier and no private material exposure.
Quarantine would atomically advance an epoch and invalidate old identity once its public wire is specified.
Request replay and provider callback identity remain distinct durable identities with one saved effect.
Concurrent use of one refresh token linearizes to at most one rotation and closes the family on reuse.
A device-revocation fence prevents later challenge approval and derived-session refresh.
Effective revocation versions are monotonic under duplicate and reordered propagation and stale verifiers fail closed.
Final approval and recovery would have one threshold transition after an approval wire is published.
LOGIN_RECONCILIATION survives worker death after the publicly observable LEASED state.
REVOCATION_PROPAGATION survives worker death without changing revocation identity or reopening a subject.
Quarantine and recovery work fencing remains blocked until incident and approval wires are published.
Key retirement is fenced and audit redelivery preserves one immutable entry identity and body after unknown acknowledgement.
A concrete V1 console workflow cannot be inferred from the published production-shell requirement.
A compromise and recovery console workflow is blocked by unpublished domain and UI wires.
OpenAPI and one point-in-time snapshot expose exact V1 resources and no secret or private material.
Audit verification detects deletion insertion reorder and payload mutation without repairing history.
FINAL migration preserves all V1 identity, replay, Work, Event and audit semantics.
Published database-time boundaries consistently govern session expiry, key retirement and revocation.
Session device user and tenant revocation affect exactly their public scope and preserve tenant isolation.
Opaque audit pagination remains stable across more than one hundred pages and closes against checkpoint and snapshot.
